title: A protocol for ultrastructural study of Candida albicans biofilm using transmission electron microscopy
protocol: Place chemically fixed biofilms of C. albicans in a Petri dish.
Cut the biofilms into 4 × 4 mm squares using a scalpel.
Insert one square of biofilm into the 200 μm cavity of a type A sample carrier filled with PBS.
Cover the type A sample carrier with a type B carrier to close the sandwich.
Freeze the sample using a Leica EM ICE high pressure freezer.
Store the type A sample carrier within a cryotube in a liquid nitrogen dewar.
Transfer biofilms from cryotubes to a flow-through ring containing 10 mL of acetone/0.2% uranyl acetate/2% methanol.
Incubate the samples in the flow-through ring at -90°C for 2 hours.
Heat up biofilms to -50°C at a rate of 20°C per hour.
Maintain samples at -50°C until the second step of UV polymerization.
Wash frozen biofilms every 20 minutes with 100% ethanol cooled at -50°C for 1 hour.
Treat ethanol used in freeze-substitution procedure with molecular sieves to remove water molecules.
Infiltrate samples with 75% ethanol/25% HM20 for 2 hours.
Infiltrate samples with 50% ethanol/50% HM20 for 16 hours.
Infiltrate samples with 25% ethanol/75% HM20 for 2 hours.
Infiltrate samples with 100% HM20 for 2 hours.
Infiltrate samples with 100% HM20 for 2 hours.
Infiltrate samples with 100% HM20 for 16 hours.
Infiltrate samples with 100% HM20 for 4 hours.
Place samples within the AFS2 apparatus under UV light at -50°C for 44 hours to allow resin polymerization.
Increase temperature from -50°C to 20°C with a slope of 10°C per hour during HM20 polymerization.
Continue HM20 polymerization under direct sunlight after reaching 20°C.
Cut samples with an ultramicrotome and arrange the sections on electron microscopy grids.
Localize the area containing C. albicans cells under a binocular microscope.
Trim the block of HM20 as a thin triangle with a razorblade.
Cut sections of 150 nm with an ultramicrotome for tomography experiments.
Cut sections of 70 nm with an ultramicrotome for immunogold labeling and contrasting.
Add a droplet of toluidine blue solution on each section.
Incubate the sections on a heat block for 5 min.
Wash thoroughly with distilled water.
Place some unstained sections on a microscope glass slide before staining them with toluidine blue.
Observe the stained sections under a light microscope to check for the presence of C. albicans biofilm cells.
Place unstained sections on a copper grid for TEM analysis after confirming the presence of fungal cells.
Avoid using the same diamond knife for cutting 150 nm and 70 nm sections to prevent damage.
Prepare 5 droplets of PBS 50 mM NH4Cl on Parafilm®.
Wash each grid in the droplets for 2 minutes.
Repeat washing step 4 times.
Incubate each grid in a droplet of blocking solution (PBS BSA 1%) for 5 minutes.
Incubate grids in 10 μL-droplets containing the primary antibody for 1 hour at room temperature.
Prepare a droplet of PBS BSA 1% that contains the primary antibody properly diluted.
Wash the grids in 10 μL-droplets of PBS BSA 0.1%.
Repeat washing step 4 times.
Wash the grids in 10 μL-droplets of PBS.
Repeat this operation 4 times.
Prepare one 10 μL-droplet of PBS BSA 1% containing protein A conjugated to 10 nm gold particles (working dilution 1/50) per grid.
Incubate the grids in the mixture for 20 min.
Wash the grids in droplets of PBS.
Repeat this operation 5 times.
Incubate the grids in droplets of PBS 1% glutaraldehyde for 5 min.
Finally, wash the grids in droplets of water.
Repeat the washes 8 times.
Contrast the grids with 4% uranyl acetate by incubating them in droplets for 30 min.
Sonicate tweezers in a water bath to remove uranyl acetate.
Wash tweezers 5 times in droplets of water.
Blot excess water from tweezers on Whatman filter paper.
Incubate grids in droplets of 2% lead citrate for 2 min.
Place sodium hydroxide pellets near lead citrate droplets to remove CO2.
Wash grids 5 times in droplets of water.
Blot excess water from grids on grade 4 Whatman filter paper.
Allow grids to air dry for at least 24 hours on a filter paper at room temperature.
Prepare a fresh aliquot of protein A-Gold particles diluted 30 times in water.
Prepare two 100 μL-droplets of diluted protein A-Gold particle per grid to be imaged using electron tomography.
Incubate each grid in the first droplet with section oriented toward the mixture for 10 min.
Wash the grids in a water drop and blot immediately on a Whatman filter paper.
Immerse each grid in the second droplet of protein A-Gold particle with section oriented toward the air and incubate for 10 min.
Wash the grids in a water drop and blot immediately on a Whatman filter paper.
Incubate the grids with sections facing down in 4% uranyl acetate droplets for 30 min.
Wash the grids 5 times in droplets of water.
Incubate the grids with sections facing down in 2% lead citrate droplets for 2 min.
Wash the grids 5 times in droplets of water and blot away the excess with a Whatman filter paper.
Let the grids dry at room temperature for 16 h before performing electron tomography.
Fill up the cryo-trap dewar of the Tecnai microscope with liquid nitrogen.
Allow the temperature of the cryo-trap to go down to −196°C.
Mount the grid on the sample holder.
Insert the sample holder in the stage of the electron microscope.
Close the column valves to maintain the vacuum of the microscope.
Verify that the objective aperture is not inserted into the microscope.
Verify that the cryo-box is not inserted into the microscope.
Open the SerialEM software for recording micrographs and acquiring tilt series.
Center the condenser aperture and bring the sample to eucentric height.
Collect a Full Grid Map (FGM) at low magnification (150×) using SerialEM.
Insert and center the objective aperture.
Find an area with fungal biofilm on the FGM and collect a Middle Magnification Map (MMM) at 2500×.
Add a marker (point) on every area of interest suitable for data acquisition on the MMM using SerialEM’s navigator.
Cook the sample by sending a total dose of 1500 electrons per square Ångström.
Refine eucentricity.
Autofocus.
Raise the magnification to 49,000×.
Launch tilt series acquisition.
Close the valves and take the sample holder out.
Rotate the grid clockwise manually through an angle of 90°.
Put back the sample holder in the stage of the electron microscope.
Redo steps 23 and 25.
Increase the stage registration in number 2 on the Navigator for the second grid insertion.
Collect a new FGM map using the updated stage coordinates.
Use registration points between new and old FGM maps to shift previous coordinates to new stage coordinates.
Collect tilt series at the same areas of interest as previously noted.
Start the tomographic reconstruction by setting up ETomo which is the graphical user interface to the IMOD package.
Enter dataset name in ETomo.
Indicate that tilt series were performed on plastic sections.
Select dual axis tomography.
Enter the size of the fiducial marker (10 nm).
Tick the box “extract tilt angles from data”.
Press the “Create Com Scripts” button to open the ETomo main window.
Go to the pre-processing section in ETomo main window.
Click sequentially on “Create Fixed Stack” and the “Use Fixed Stack” buttons.
Go to the coarse alignment section and click on the “Calculate Cross-Correlation” button.
Press the “Generate Coarse Aligned Stack” button.
Track gold particles on all sections of the tilt series to generate the fiducial model.
Refine gold particle tracking with the help of residual errors in every section of the tilt series.
Sample three regions of the tomogram (top, middle, and bottom parts of the tilt series) by pressing “Create Sample Tomograms”.
Add the top and bottom surfaces from every reconstruction by pressing the “Create Boundary Models” button.
Press on “Compute Z shift and Pitch Angles” button to fit the reconstruction into the smallest volume possible.
Generate the tomogram of the axis A using Weighted Back Projection (WBP).
Reconstruct the tomogram corresponding to the second axis (B axis).
Do the pre-processing for the B-axis dataset.
Perform coarse alignment on the B-axis dataset.
Use transferfid to create a seed model for the B axis based on fiducial points from axis A.
Track gold particles throughout all sections of the tilt series for the B-axis.
Generate the fiducial model linked to the B-axis.
Fill gaps with the bead fixer.
Create command files for running different programs used for the combine procedure.
Press the “Start Combine” button.
Press the “Open Combined Volume” to visualize the final tomogram.
Trim the volume of the final tomogram along the X, Y, and Z axes.
Cleanup intermediate files.
